questions.prompt: Explain why the volume of a cylinder is its base area multiplied by its height.
questions.modelAnswer: A cylinder can be thought of as a stack of thin circular layers, like coins. Each layer has area πr², and there are enough layers to fill the height h. So the volume is the area of one layer times the height: πr² × h. This is the same idea as a cuboid, which is layers of l × b stacked h high.
